text:
Ava R.: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's canary we saw p99 spikes for streaming responses when partial-decode + aggressive batching are enabled. Put raw profiling here: KV miss rate jumps ~3x and we observe kernel pin thrash around token budgets.

Liang W.: Ugh — did the canary enable the new backpressure smoothing?

Ava R.: Yes, `stream_backpressure_smoothing=1` + token budget target=96. Baseline before change: p99 ~210ms. Canary: p99 ~420ms on some configs.

Priya S.: Any flamegraphs or perf logs?

Ava R.: Pasted snippet from perf tool (trimmed):
```
flame: decode_loop -> kv_lookup -> kernel_switch (hot) -> wait_for_batch_slot -> partial_decode
KV cache: hit_rate=0.78 -> 0.45 during spike
avg batch_size: 6 -> 13 during spike
```

Mateo G.: So batch size increased (good for throughput) but kv hit rate tanked and kernel switching increased — that suggests the smoothing heuristic is coalescing requests across different model variants or seq-lens. Could be mixing short chat with long completion and causing kv warmup thrash.

Liang W.: We pin kernels based on dominant seq length in a window. If smoothing expands window too wide, we might be grouping incompatible seq lengths. Maybe need to add a seq-length affinity threshold.

Priya S.: Agreed. Propose: keep backpressure smoothing but cap coalesce window to N tokens or M ms per request type. e.g. `max_coalesce_tokens=256, coalesce_time_ms=18`. Also prefer partial-decode preemption for long-running sequences.

Ava R.: Sketching a config patch I tried locally (worked on tiny sim, still noisy in env):
```yaml
streaming:
  backpressure_smoothing: true
  max_coalesce_tokens: 256   # new cap
  coalesce_time_ms: 20      # conservative
  seq_len_affinity: 0.25    # 0..1, lower -> tighter grouping
  partial_decode_preempt: true
```

Nina (eng-runtime): Did you correlate with kernel selection logs? Which kernels flipped?

Ava R.: Yes — logs show repeated flip between `matmul_opt_v2` and `matmul_smallkern` every ~200ms on the same worker during spike. Kernel swap cost adds ~6-8ms, plus cache misses.

Mateo G.: That explains the p99. Kernel swap plus cold KV = compounding latency. Two-pronged mitigation: 1) Avoid coalescing across kernel affinity boundaries; 2) Add lightweight warmup probing when a new kernel is chosen (cheap KV warmup).

Liang W.: For (1) we can compute a kernel-affinity signature per request: (model_variant, seq_bucket, dtype_hint). If score distance > threshold, don't coalesce. Cheap to compute. For (2) warmup probe could be 1-token dummy decode to prefill KV for that kernel path. Cost ~1ms but prevents p99 blast.

Priya S.: Sounds reasonable. But warmup probes add overhead if done too often — maybe only do them when we detect >2 kernel flips within 5s on the same worker.

Ava R.: Ran a microtest with affinity gating + single-probe-on-flip. Results: p99 down from 420ms -> 230ms, kv hit rate back to 0.72, batch size stable ~7. Throughput dip negligible.

Mateo G.: Nice. Any regressions on tail for long conversations? We should run a 2h soak with chat-heavy traffic to ensure we don't break streaming steady-state.

Liang W.: I'll queue a canary with these settings to the staging fleet. Can we also add better tracing so we can see: 
- coalesce decisions (why joined/skip)
- kernel-affinity score
- probe events

Ava R.: Already added quick tags to the span: `coalesce_reason`, `affinity_score`, `probe_sent`. Plan to roll with 1% canary.

infra-bot: Canary deployment triggered: canary-id=cb-2026-03-18-17, targets=staging-* (1%).

Priya S.: Also let's instrument KV metrics per-model-variant + per-worker so we can detect localized thrash. Current metrics are aggregated and hide noisy nodes.

Ava R.: Good call — added `kv_hit_rate{worker,model_variant}`. Will upload dashboards after canary starts.

Mateo G.: If staging looks good, let's plan prod rollout as: 1) affinity gating only (gradual 5->25->100%), 2) enable probe-on-flip after stability window. Avoid enabling time-based coalesce changes at same time.

Liang W.: Agreed. I'll prepare the rollout plan + quick rollback steps (flip flag to old smoothing).

Ava R.: Thanks all. If you see p99 regressions please ping me directly and include `trace_id`.

Priya S.: One last note — partial-decode scheduling: we should prefer scheduling short partial-decodes ahead of long ones when flush cadence is tight. I.e., add short-first priority when we've hit partial-decode backlog > X. Otherwise long ops hog the kernel.

Mateo G.: That's the short-first heuristic we discussed earlier. Add it to the canary as an opt-in flag: `partial_decode_priority=short_first_threshold=3`

Liang W.: I'll add both flags to the canary config. Rolling now.

Ava R.: Thanks team :thumbsup:
